## Answers and evidence

- Exact composition: `generate.mjs:547-560,604-608` produces the standalone page by replacing exactly one data-script tag in the already-headered index page. Its inline script is byte-identical to the generated data file. Independent scratch runs verified both headers, exact replacement, deterministic bytes, no script src, and explicit refusal of zero or two matching tags.
- Escaping: the stable serializer JSON-quotes keys and string values before replacing every literal less-than character. No payload can supply an HTML script end tag or comment opener. Independent probes round-tripped 22 strings in keys and values, including mixed-case close tags, whitespace/slash delimiters, comment openers/closers, quotes, backslashes, lone surrogates, and U+2028/U+2029. Those Unicode characters are valid string contents in ES2019+; a plain `-->` inside the JSON string neither closes a script nor escapes the string. Standards cross-check: WHATWG HTML script-data tokenization and restrictions on script contents; ECMA-262 String Literals / TC39 Subsume JSON.
- Browser proof: headless Google Chrome opened the actual standalone file in a directory with no sibling data file, using an isolated temporary profile and DNS disabled. It rendered 271 map SVG nodes. A combined mixed-case close-tag, img/onerror, comment, U+2028/U+2029 payload remained text in the title; no injected image appeared. The first browser oracle incorrectly searched script source as well as rendered markup; narrowing it to the viewport fixed that probe-only false positive.
- Existing outputs: replaying the base generator and head generator against the original base fixture gives byte-identical index and data files. With hostile less-than data, only the data's source representation changes; evaluated values are identical. Generate stdout now names the extra file. `open` still selects index.html.
- Mutation: removing the escape in a copied generator makes all three dependency-free equivalents of the committed golden, standalone-equality, and hostile-boundary assertions fail. The golden fixture itself contains escaped less-than bytes and no literal less-than. This independently verifies the oracle; it is not a claim that local Vitest ran.
- Filesystem/privacy: the standalone file uses the same output directory and `writeFresh` path as the existing files. Scratch outputs all had mode 0644 under the current umask. A pre-existing standalone symlink was replaced by a regular file and its target stayed untouched. The changed fixture/golden/test payloads are synthetic; no secret, token, private identity, or home path was found in the committed fixtures.
- D-F252-1: the sixth-strike count matches D-167-1 plus D-36-1, D-171-1, D-229-1, and D-F214-1. The main checkout's generator is currently clean, consistent with the recorded restoration. The historical edit/move command sequence is the coder's account, not independently witnessed; no contradiction found.
- Cost: no loop, poll, timer, hook, or launch was added or changed. Existing on-demand collection is unchanged; incremental cost is one serialization replacement and one extra page write per invocation, not per-seat recurring work.
